Pablo: No wonder he was an artistic genius. Pablo thinks fast and laterally, and as such he alters course in a flash. He is a good friend and a diabolical enemy.
Paddo: The Fluid Link Man. Paddo is as knowledgeable and savvy as a sewer rat and he has the weird knack of unconsciously gravitating people towards him.
Paige: Yes, Paige is a man. Paige is a good man. And he’s quietly spoken.
Paolo: What? He’s prone to fits of sensationalism? Nooooo…..surely not! (Unless of course he’s a fucking astronaut, in which case I think we all agree there’s no need for him to say or do anything to get our attention.)
Paris: Paris isn’t from France and his hands are hard from hard work, and hand moisturiser is none of his business unless he’s alone and feeling horny. He doesn’t tend to fools and he can look after himself if need be. Whether he’s small in stature or not he’s usually the largest man in the room because he is honourable and has integrity, although he rarely stops at one beer.
Parish: The Mysterious Good Guy. Parish achieves great things but he seems to do it under the cover of perpetual darkness because no one ever actually sees him do anything. How do you do it, Parish?
Parker: The Rat! Very smart, Parker thinks on his feet and, if ever there is some massive catastrophic event effecting thousands, he is never one of the first casualties. Probably not one of the last, either.
Parko: Serene and good-humoured, Parko presents a shining example of good grace and wisdom to his kids. Best of all he'll never fully grow up.
Pascal: Good friends with Gideon, Pascal is the artist's artist. True to his chosen form of expression, Pascal is intensely passionate about what he does, just as he is for anyone who tries their best.
Pasco: Pasco is a fucking lightning bolt. Can you smell the ozone? Don't play golf with him. Amen.
Pasty: An outboard motor mechanic from some far flung island outpost, and pound for pound one of the funniest people on earth. If questioned about his method of feeding his dogs he’ll reply with the following statement: “All you do is put out the dog nuts and they’ll eat ‘em. Eventually they’ll keep comin’ back. What else can they do?”
Pat: Far more naive than his female counterpart, if Pat isn’t a rather innocent kind of fellow then he is thin-skinned. If this is the case then he will try to look relaxed and cool but in actual fact he will complain more than anyone.
Patrick: Patrick is a little toy chimpanzee powered by AA batteries who bangs his symbols together for hours, making an irritating, “Patrick, Patrick, Patrick, Patrick,” noise, that drives you mental. Later, when he grows up, he becomes a rude doctor with a shocking bedside manner, who gets very angry when the women he fancies don’t fancy him back.
Paul: Paul is an interesting persona. A polite man whose depths sometimes take years to see, he’s intelligent enough, normal enough and he almost never falls ill. To maintain a perfect balance in his life, however, he must perform some semi-evil act every six months. Paul is a deceptively tall name and without some kind of dirty little secret to keep him real, he’d just topple over.
Pauly: Pauly rhymes with Can I Help You?  Thus, he’s always there, and he’ll do anything to help anyone who needs it.
Pavo: Rarely does Pavo take no for an answer, and if he does it means he’s exhausted all other avenues of reprieve. Many consider him to be a physically tough individual and this is probably true, but he is fair, and perhaps this is the toughest aspect of him of all: to be objective and to keep trying, until he realises he shouldn’t or can’t. Strong family values.
Pax: Some people are just plain cool. You can't manufacture it, you can't bottle it and it's very hard to grow. Pax has it in spades. The only question is, how is he using it? Mmm?
Pearce:
Pearce, get away from that fucking mirror, will you? Now, get outside and get your hands dirty because germs are good for you. 
The end.
Peck: Like a contented and graceful waterbird, Peck may look like he's standing around doing nothing but this is not the case. Rarely prone to fits of melancholy, if someone or something is to his disliking, Peck's facial expression will hardly alter. All that will happen is that he'll spread his wings regally, wait for the first lick of breeze and then lift off to somewhere more welcoming, barely without a sound. Peck.
Pedro: Be it in an illicit or legitimate trade in which he’s involved, Pedro is prepared to get his hands dirty while at the same time existing in the upper echelons.
Percic: Most men of Adriatic decent are sure of themselves and of their decisions, but cheerful Percic is a little bit different. If questioned about his parentage by somebody in a jovial manner, for example, he won’t immediately assume that he needs to kill them.
Percy: Often quite tall, Percy is rarely rattled and his conversations with women are usually risqué.
Peregrine: If he isn’t a trifle goofy and light-hearted, then there is an excellent chance he is English and an arrogant cock head.
Perko: The affable man-about-town. He rarely sleeps around and never says anything bad about anyone unless it is wholly deserved, and where it’s airing actually achieves something. He may not have finished high school, but Perko works hard and is a rock for most of his friends.
Pero: Pero is a knowledgeable, thinking individual who takes only a moment to size up most situations – lethal or otherwise – and he’s always ready to act, holding only as much fear in his heart as he needs to keep him thinking efficiently.
Perry: The bottom button on a shirt as worn by Alastair. He is secretly devastated when he gets tucked-in because he can’t see anything and this happens all the time. Spoilt as a child.
Peter: His name is older than the rocks but he always has plenty of energy, which might explain why he’s the butt of many jokes and the cornerstone of many buildings. How did you pull that off Pete? I’m still trying to figure it out.
Peters: As a result of constantly explaining his name properly he has learned to turn everything into a joke, which is handy given his quite ambitious nature. Unpredictably fun in the bedroom
Petros: Petros is no stargazer, but he does keep an eagle eye on his employees inside his fruit factory. He pays them well, but he just likes to keep an eye on things.
Pez: As a bouncer with a degree in Greek philosophy, Pez is a big guy whose dangerous eyes shield a soft heart.
Philip:
(Before we begin Philip, we need to tell you that you and the double-L version are identical, so suck it up.)
Anyway, where were we? Ah yes…Philip has read more books than he has hit some kind of ball with some kind of bat, implement. Indeed, what is sport? On the flip side he is so intellectual that he wouldn't enjoy how that third sentence was constructed at all, although he’s smart enough to have followed the thread of what we're on about. It's a weird world, eh? In summation, we can tell you that Philip (and his double-L cousin) is something of a conservative man. Is he a bore? Well, that's a good question. We can say that he does like the sound of his own voice.
Philippe: Once the President of the University Wine Appreciation Society, Philippe finished his Ph.D, worked for a bit, then gave it away so he could follow his passion of learning about Shibari. We suggest you look it up. The moral to the story is that he is one deep-thinking man, funny too, who takes every path in life to the very end, sexual play included.
Phillip: No, he's not a boring poo-poo man. He's the same as Philip, with one L. So, head on up there brother and we'll see you in the pavillion after the game.
Phillipe: A king amongst his peers. He counsels, he’s a confidante and he is a salve for all those who need one. His deep-thinking approach to all issues means he experiments beyond the norm and this only adds weight to his quest - to seek meaning and significance here in this thing we call Life.
Phoenix: Pheonix nearly drowned in surf that was way too big for him. His friends, who could handle themselves, tried to tell him but there’s just no getting through to some people.
Pi: If he thought it would do you any good, Pi would tell you that genius is the loneliest ticket in the world.
Pidzy: Film maker. Father. Comedian. Remarkable facial hair. No idea about this thing called money let alone fiscal responsibility.
Piero: A stickler for tradition, Piero's parents instilled in him a duty to care after his family and loved ones. Truth be known his wife is better at it than he is, but he pretends to be in control sometimes. Piero has a mischievous side that MUST be indulged from time to time. And he'll tell you: what is life if it isn't fun?
Piers: For something different, Piers will often masturbate while wearing a condom. He calls it practice.
Pieter: Well, yes, he is something of a Peter, but his European bent means he is far more adherent to methods and systems which are proven to work. And if they don't work he'll almost certainly never employ them again. He makes a capable sailor, a fair and friendly leader and a caring and humorous partner, who, albeit, is occasionally quite stubborn.
Pig: Self-assured. Not the chauvinist we were led to believe at all.
Piggy: Piggy is outgoing and a friend to all, but like many of his colleagues he is a nightmare when he’s pissed.
Pip: Rarely overweight, Pip darts around like Muhammad Ali in the ring, and his actions are nearly always aimed at some kind of creative outlet. Pip is no plumber although his active brain means he might own a building company, which is about as close to plumbing as he’d ever get.
Pippin: The city wannabe hipster, minus the beard. Trendy spectacles adorn his face and his scarves are sometimes worn in quite warm weather. He’ll tell you there’s nothing wrong with possessing a little style, and he may be right. Our only question is that which is untested: In a life and death situation could you turn to him for advice? And you might be surprised with the answer…
Pissup: Pissup is constructed of sturdy moral fibre and he tells a perfectly intricate story –  missing no details whatsoever – that always finishes unpredictably.
PJ: A jolly man who, only recently, learnt to buy his own underpants.
PK: No mountain is too big. P.K is relaxed and perceptive and he does most things in an above-average fashion. Self-promotion: he doesn’t need it. His actions and attitude do the calling and there endeth the lesson.
Pook: Originally from somewhere near South Africa, Pook is centred, calm and forgiving like an oily flat ocean and the universe thus allows him to do anything he wants. Nice work Pook.
Pope: Pope is the kind of bloke who goes to the Melbourne Cup on his own, knowing no one, and by 5pm is $10,000 up, and best mates with the winning jockey.
Porter: Money is attracted to this fellow because people trust him. He’d make a good white collar crim’.
Portland:
"Oh no, I quite like visiting the dump, as a matter of fact. The smell isn't that bad, and you'd be amazed what you can find."

Portland is proof artistry lies in the most obscure places, sometimes.
Possum:
Q: How can any man feel empowered and dynamic when called such a thing? 
A: …Exactly. 
The result is a cuddly, funny bastard who has a perpetual smile stuck to his face. He does get sad, but only because, unlike many men, he gives full scope to his emotions. The men of the world could definitely learn a lot from his example.

(Note: Women, by and large, don’t really need the lesson because they are far more advanced in this arena.)
Prescott: Jesus Prescott, go and sit over there in the corner with Bruno and Bindi. Thank you.
Preston: Here is another who believes that the world was made for them, although Preston doesn’t understand why walking around with his thumb up his own arse looks weird. It’s his God-given right, after all.
Presty: Intelligent and sensitive, as well as being very funny, Presty is here for the long haul. Always one to take a bullet for the team, he occasionally suffers the long fight more than most. But, he keeps his chin up because above all else he is the perennial optimist.
Provan: Like a river that has moods known only unto itself, Provan is his own creature. If he's a city cat then he comes out only at night, and if he's a country boy then he'll barely stay in the one spot for more than a few days. Solitude: he's good at it. If he is that country boy, and let's hope he is, he rarely wears a watch, he gets up with the first birds and he knows everything about the seasons, rock formations and the flood plains. If he's that city cat, he's got dark hair and he doesn't trust just anyone.
Ptolemy: Is Ptolemy into astronomy, anyone? Seriously, is he? The stars or the cards? Anyway, he’s a nice fella’ who wears plenty of amulets and bracelets, etc.
Puke: Now Puke, you know we like you, okay? You have friends who adore you, you seem to make the right decisions most of the time and you're far more dedicated than your name leads us to believe, but how can we send you to this conference in Japan if you insist on being called Puke? Most of them speak English mate, and they know what a puke is. Are you on my wavelength, chief? (By the way, it's your shout.)
Pumpkin: Pumpkin is the sort of man that gets married in scarlett. He'll tell you he married a Princess.
Pussy: Like a wild male lion on the savannah that has just injested a gob-full of ecstacy and cocaine, all Pussy is concerned about is cuddling up to any creature he can find, before declaring his undying love. Zebra, gnu, hyena, landcruiser - he doesn't care. He's just so full of love and purring bliss that he can barely contain himself.
